scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Across 2440 tickets, median response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, versus a 3.0-day SLA.

F-03.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-04.statement: The billing-db tariff change log contains 0 records, i.e. no tariff change is on record for the relevant period.

F-05.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 used an ESTIMATED read and 1785 used an ACTUAL read (billing-db, E-05).

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, but execution requires Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: 320 accounts were on an ESTIMATED read in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (billing-db).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: Dispute volume doubled because Customer Service cannot respond fast enough to tickets, not because bills are actually wrong; faster/automated ticket answering would resolve the surge.

H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed/accepted incorrectly, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-GAP.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery to billing degraded (vendor export issue), causing more missing-read estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter-read completion dropped (e.g., staffing), increasing missing reads that get estimated and billed incorrectly.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-FAULT.statement: The estimate-substitution logic itself (used when no accepted read exists) is miscalibrated or over-triggered, producing inaccurate bills independent of which upstream source failed.

H-GENUINE-USAGE-CHANGE.statement: Bills are largely correct; the surge reflects a genuine increase in billed consumption (e.g., seasonal/tariff) that customers dispute as 'wrong' without an actual billing defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM ticket data (2440 tickets) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both comfortably within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating Customer Service is not failing to respond to tickets quickly. This undercuts the premise that ticket response slowness drives the dispute surge, pointing instead toward an underlying billing-accuracy issue.

CRM dispute volume by month shows a sudden step-change at the August boundary (Jun 610, Jul 590, Aug 1180, Sep 1260) rather than a gradual rise, i.e. volume roughly doubled in a single month and held at the new level into September.

Field route completion for the Aug-Sep 2026 period was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, with 9200 manual-read accounts in scope — a shortfall in manual meter-read collection coinciding with the dispute surge window, but the record does not show the pre-August baseline completion rate or tie the shortfall directly to disputed bills.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff change is on record for the dispute-surge period, which rules out a tariff adjustment as the driver of a genuine-but-disputed consumption increase.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) used an ACTUAL read and only 1240 (41%) used an ESTIMATED read, so most disputed bills were NOT produced via missing-read estimate substitution. This weakens any causal story that locates the surge primarily in estimate substitution (AMI gap, field-read gap, estimate logic) and points more toward a defect affecting billing/import of accepted reads generally.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field routes have been short three readers since July, causing late route completion and estimated bills for affected customers; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not a measured fact, and SH-FIELD has a stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward attributing problems to staffing.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, which agrees with E-04's authoritative billing-db record showing zero tariff-change-log entries for the period. As a non-authoritative stakeholder statement it corroborates rather than adds new decision-relevant information, reinforcing that the genuine-usage/tariff explanation of the dispute surge remains unsupported.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager confirmation, which is the documentary basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update; it does not speak to the billing dispute surge's causal mechanism.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query shows 320 accounts received an ESTIMATED read in the most recent billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but the returned fields (account_id, route only) carry no read-type/dispute/tariff/import-status linkage. Standalone, this count cannot be tied to the disputed-bills population or to the import-rule-change mechanism.

U-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Treat H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE as unconfirmed; do not notify Billing Operations of a confirmed root cause until the rule-change log query completes.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.question: Is vendor-provisioned MDMS export access available to pull AMI read events for the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputed bills?

U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the field route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-03) explain any portion of the 41% ESTIMATED-read disputed bills?

U-FIELD-READ-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat field-read completion as a non-dominant, unconfirmed secondary factor; do not elevate route_completion_recovery above TARGET status.

U-DISPUTE-BASELINE-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects the numeric target used in the dispute-volume-recovery success criterion; a wrong baseline could set an unachievable or too-lenient threshold.
U-DISPUTE-BASELINE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Review pre-August ticket categorization in crm-tickets to estimate the non-import-related baseline dispute rate.
U-DISPUTE-BASELINE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use the observed Jun-Jul average (~600/month) as a provisional baseline pending finer categorization.

A-SINGLE-DOMINANT-CAUSE.statement: The dispute surge has one dominant causal mechanism rather than multiple concurrent contributors (e.g. an import defect plus a smaller field-read contribution).

A-ROUTE-COMPLETION-UNRELATED.statement: The field route completion shortfall coincides with but does not materially drive the dispute surge, given most disputed bills used ACTUAL reads.

proposal.root_problem: Since August 2026 Lakeside Water's billing dispute ticket volume stepped up from ~600/month to ~1200+/month and has held at that level (E-02). The sole currently-supported mechanism, H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE, holds that a billing import/validation defect around August causes bills computed from accepted meter reads to be processed incorrectly, triggering disputes — evidenced by 59% of disputed bills using an ACTUAL (not ESTIMATED) read (E-05), which rules out missing-read estimate substitution as the dominant cause while response speed (E-01) and tariff changes (E-04/E-07) are also ruled out.
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) requested building an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills" (CL-01) — this framing (response-handling) is CONTRADICTED by E-01 and is treated as an unverified requester hypothesis, not the problem itself.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume stepped from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200+/month (Aug-Sep 2026), a sudden step-change rather than a gradual rise (E-02).
Ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA), so Customer Service responsiveness is not degraded (E-01).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) used an ACTUAL meter read rather than an ESTIMATED one, so most disputes are not explained by missing-read estimate substitution (E-05).

Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts, a shortfall coinciding with the surge window but not shown to directly explain disputed bills (E-03).
No tariff change is on record for the period (E-04), corroborated by SH-BILL (E-07), ruling out a tariff-driven genuine consumption/billing change.
causal_chain: Around August 2026 something in billing import/validation processing of accepted meter reads begins causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE).
Most of these incorrectly processed bills come from ACTUAL reads, not from missing-read ESTIMATED substitutions (E-05).
Customers receiving these bills perceive them as wrong and file dispute tickets.
Dispute ticket volume steps up sharply at the August boundary and holds into September (E-02), consistent with a discrete process/rule change rather than a slow drift.
Customer Service, which is already responding within SLA (E-01), cannot resolve the surge by speeding up responses, because the underlying bills themselves are wrong, not the response process.

assumptions.statement: Elimination of response-speed, tariff change, and estimate-substitution-driven causes implies the surge's dominant mechanism is a billing import/validation defect affecting accepted reads, though this is inferred by elimination rather than directly observed in the rule-change log.
The field route completion shortfall coincides with but does not materially drive the dispute surge, given most disputed bills used ACTUAL reads.
The dispute surge has one dominant causal mechanism rather than multiple concurrent contributors (e.g. an import defect plus a smaller field-read contribution).
